questions.q: Which labelled great vessel emerges from the right ventricle and carries deoxygenated blood towards the lungs?
questions.explain: The pulmonary trunk arises from the right ventricle and divides into right and left pulmonary arteries. The aorta arises from the left ventricle and carries oxygenated blood to the systemic circulation.
questions.alt: Anterior view of the heart in situ with the great vessels, pericardium, lungs and diaphragm labelled.

questions.q: The heart is enclosed by the pericardium shown in the image. Which part of the pericardium is tough, fibrous and limits acute over-distension of the heart?
questions.explain: The fibrous pericardium is the strong outer connective-tissue sac. It anchors the heart and helps prevent sudden over-distension. The serous pericardium has parietal and visceral layers.
